back: An independent examination of the financial statements by an auditor appointed by the shareholders, ending with an opinion on whether they give a true and fair view.
External: independent, appointed by shareholders, reports on the statements. Internal: employed by management, reports on controls and operations.
Unqualified; qualified (material but limited); adverse (material and pervasive); disclaimer (no opinion because evidence is missing).
The duty of directors to look after the shareholders' funds, use them in their interests and report honestly on how they have been used.

front: What does a **true and fair view** mean?
back: The statements are free of material misstatement and follow accounting standards and the law, so users can rely on them.
Rotate the audit partner, use separate teams, refuse conflicting work, report pressure to the board, disclose and dispose of shares.
It gives reasonable assurance, not a guarantee: it uses samples, relies on management's information and looks backwards.
A matter is material if omitting or misstating it could change the decisions of users of the statements.
